note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after 05646d85eb dropped the always-true hasCA/hasCert stubs from ValidatePKIRefs (existence now a ze:reference at config load). RFC 7296 Section 2.16 re-read in rfc/full/rfc7296.txt: "For this reason, these protocols are typically used to authenticate the initiator to the responder and MUST be used in conjunction with a public-key-signature-based authentication of the responder to the initiator." The two changed units keep their inputs and assertions: TestEapAuthConfigRejectsEAPWithoutCertificate requires ValidatePKIRefs to refuse an eap-mschapv2 and an eap-tls peer with no certificate, naming the peer, 'certificate' and 'RFC 7296 Section 2.16', and to accept the same peer once a certificate is named; TestEapAuthConfigAcceptsPreSharedKeyPeer requires a pre-shared-secret peer to pass. Read at the producer: ipsec/validate.go ValidatePKIRefs still refuses IsEAPMode with an empty Auth.Certificate before any lookup, so the stubs never decided the outcome. The unchanged units still cover the wire: the EAP responder AUTH is an RFC 7427 signature verified under the certificate key, computeServerAuth refuses no-cert EAP at setup, and the initiator refuses a PSK AUTH from an EAP responder. Q1-Q4 unchanged from the earlier judgement: EAP responder AUTH is a public-key signature, no-cert EAP refused at setup and config, PSK peers unaffected.
